subject.title: fix(plugins): deep-clone registry snapshot so nested mutations roll back (#107514)

question: Should plugin-registration rollback promise deep restoration for arbitrary plugin-provided class instances, or restrict the registry snapshot contract to cloneable canonical data plus explicit owner-defined handling for opaque objects?
rationale: JavaScript cannot generically recreate all class instances safely: prototype reconstruction does not restore private slots, non-enumerable state, or constructor invariants. Choosing which values the registry may own is a compatibility contract decision.

options.title: Narrow the clone contract
options.body: Recommended: deep-clone known mutable registry data and require explicit owner handling for opaque/custom instances, avoiding invalid reconstructed objects.

options.title: Add an explicit clone protocol
options.body: Define and document a registry-value cloning contract so plugin-owned classes can provide a valid rollback snapshot.

options.title: Accept prototype-only reconstruction
options.body: Keep the current behavior and accept that custom classes with private or non-enumerable state are unsupported in rollback snapshots.

recommendation.title: Narrow the clone contract
recommendation.body: Recommended: deep-clone known mutable registry data and require explicit owner handling for opaque/custom instances, avoiding invalid reconstructed objects.

likelyOwner.reason: This requires a core/plugin compatibility decision rather than selecting among mechanically equivalent fixes.
